input: I'm profiling a Vulkan application on a mobile GPU using Android GPU Inspector and I see a recurring GPU stall of ~3 ms every 16th frame. The render graph uses a tile-based deferred rendering (TBDR) approach with a G-buffer pass followed by a lighting subpass. The AGP report flags 'external dependency flush' between the geometry and lighting subpasses. I've already merged them into a single render pass with proper subpass dependencies (VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT). What other render pass or framebuffer attachment configurations could still force an on-chip tile eviction and cause this periodic stall?
